payload.claim: This test's docstring claims 'every cell's teardown removes its own network', but the final assertions (418-431) only check the subnets that `allocate_network` returned at claim time and their pairwise disjointness; they never check `network_model` after `_reverify_stubbed` finishes, so no assertion confirms any of the four networks (first_baseline, second_baseline, second_head, or the outer run's own head) was actually removed by its cell's `finally`. Deleting the `runtime.remove_network(network)` call in `_gate_cell`'s finally block (package.py) leaves every one of this test's assertions green: `claimed` is populated at claim time regardless of later cleanup, and `allocate_network`'s own collision handling still keeps the four subnets disjoint even when stale entries are left live in the model. Contrast this with the sibling test in tests/test_session.py (`test_two_gate_only_cells_at_once...`), which does assert `second_network not in network_model` and `first_network not in network_model` after each cell's `with` block exits — this test has no equivalent check.
